memory_candidates.content: When a documentation task runs concurrently with sibling implementation tasks touching the same subsystem, re-read the shared file(s) with `git status --short` + `git diff`/`git log` immediately before each edit and immediately before final verification, not just once at dispatch start. Content the plan/research asked to be documented as an open gap can become closed (committed) mid-dispatch by a concurrent sibling; the honest response is to rewrite the affected sections to describe the current state (with a 'why this closure is/isn't a proof' framing consistent with the document's own thesis), not to ship a claim the same working tree already contradicts.

When two concurrently-dispatched agents may both edit the same file in a shared working tree, and your own edit's insertion point risks landing adjacent to their uncommitted hunk, anchor your Edit at a textually distant, stable location in the file (e.g. a section's opening rather than its end) so `git diff` naturally produces non-adjacent hunks. This lets `git status`/`git diff` review stay legible and avoids a whole-file `git add` inadvertently staging a sibling's in-progress uncommitted work under your own commit message.
